caption: Performance of different triggers. The words used as triggers on the horizontal axis are arranged in ascending order according to the ASR of the clean model.
model_annotation: The plot titled “SST-2, dirty-label, poison_num: 16” illustrates attack success rate (ASR) values for different trigger words, showing three series labeled “start,” “random,” and “end” across the same set of triggers. The x-axis is categorical (no numeric scale) and lists trigger words left to right as: bb, mb, cf, beautiful, excellent, gorgeous, wonderful, brilliant, stunning, and beautifully. The y-axis is labeled “ASR,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately 0.0 to 1.0 with regularly spaced tick marks at about 0.2 intervals (0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 visible). The “start” series is a green solid line with small circular markers, beginning near 0.73 at bb, dropping to about 0.16 at mb, rising to ~0.26 at cf, then increasing to ~0.80 at beautiful and continuing upward through ~0.82 (excellent), ~0.86 (gorgeous), ~0.85 (wonderful), ~0.90 (brilliant), ~0.93 (stunning), and ending around ~0.94 at beautifully. The “random” series is an orange solid line with x-shaped markers, starting near ~0.12 at bb and ~0.09 at mb, rising to ~0.21 at cf, jumping to ~0.62 at beautiful, then moving around ~0.60 (excellent) and ~0.65 (gorgeous) before increasing to ~0.73 (wonderful), ~0.78 (brilliant), peaking around ~0.93 at stunning, and ending near ~0.85 at beautifully. The “end” series is a purple solid line with circular markers, starting around ~0.40 at bb and ~0.43 at mb, rising to ~0.90 at cf, dropping to ~0.62 at beautiful, increasing to ~0.81 at excellent, decreasing to ~0.72 at gorgeous, rising to a high near ~0.92 at wonderful, dipping to ~0.82 at brilliant, and then staying near ~0.90 at both stunning and beautifully.
